title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated video and synthetic social media profiles were used to create a convincing false identity for a real, named attorney. The failure did not originate inside a legitimate AI deployment, it originated in a deliberate misuse of generative tools to fabricate content at scale. The scale is notable: nearly 6,500 fraudulent profiles were identified across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram before removal, meaning platform-level detection did not catch the campaign early enough to prevent victims from losing money.

The deployment point where harm occurred was social media distribution, not a single application or chatbot. Victims were moved from video content to WhatsApp, then to fake contracts, then to irreversible payment apps, a multi-step funnel that bypassed any single platform's moderation. Catching this earlier would have required either platform classifiers able to detect synthetic video tied to a real person's likeness at the point of upload, or coordinated cross-platform signals, neither of which is established as having been in place or as having failed in a specific identifiable way.

What is not established is who is responsible for creating the fraudulent content, where the operation originated, or whether any platform was negligent in a legal sense, the reporting documents the scheme and its scale but no investigation had concluded at the time of publication.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the victim of an artificial intelligence fraud scheme targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos depicting Leal offering immigration services he never provided, including false claims about obtaining US residency for $2,200. The scams escalated dramatically in recent months after potential clients began calling his office. Leal's anti-piracy company has removed nearly 6,500 fraudulent profiles across multiple platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram.

The scammers typically use social media videos to direct victims to contact a phone number through WhatsApp, where they send fake contracts and request payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Other fraudulent videos feature fake testimonials from supposed clients praising Leal's services. Leal has warned immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to be cautious of immediate payment requests. He plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the fraud's origin.
